## 1. What you will get

This notebook prepares an explicit rectangular CPW cross-section for AEDT Q2D
and reads its returned per-unit-length capacitance, conductance, inductance,
and resistance matrices. The cross-section is authored from stated dimensions;
SCGSim does not infer a slice from a GDS or 3D layout.

![Declared Q2D CPW cross-section: silicon substrate, signal, and two reference-ground rectangles. Vertical scale is enlarged to show the 0.2 µm metal thickness; this is source geometry, not a solver result.](../assets/q2d-cross-section.svg){#fig-q2d-cpw-cross-section}

The model uses a 200 µm wide by 500 µm thick Si substrate, a 10 µm Nb signal,
two 40 µm Nb grounds, 10 µm gaps, and 0.2 µm metal thickness. The
[OrcaPen Q2D notebook](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9/notebooks/CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_q2d.ipynb)
is the PDK-owned cross-section example.

## 2. Prepare your environment

Use Python 3.12 or 3.13. Install Git and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/),
then create a study environment with the pinned SCGSim and OrcaPen source.

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 cpw-line-parameters
cd cpw-line-parameters
uv add 'scgsim[aedt] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@90fb50ef9de80fa6e556d2f2a09fb45707efeea0' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9' \
  ipykernel
uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('scgsim')); print(version('orpen-sc-pdk'))"
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab
```

SCGSim is pinned to `2.0.0rc11`; the selected public PDK source is pinned to
`35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9` and imports as `orpen_sc_pdk`.
Install AEDT 2023.2 or 2024.2, PyAEDT 1.3.0, and an available license on the
solver host. Python packages prepare the request; they do not install AEDT.

Check: both package versions print, and Jupyter uses this project's `.venv`.

## 3. Choose your settings

Edit the central settings before preparing a new run. Rectangle positions and
sizes are in micrometres; the setup frequency is in GHz. The four-value Q2D
Region padding order is `(+X, -X, +Y, -Y)`.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-settings
from pathlib import Path

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # Select 2023.2 or 2024.2 for the licensed host.
OUTPUT_DIR = Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-q2d")
PROJECT_NAME = "public_cpw_q2d"
DESIGN_NAME = "CpwFiniteGroundQ2d"
SETUP_NAME = "Setup1"
FREQUENCY_GHZ = 6.0
MAXIMUM_PASSES = 3
REGION_PADDING_UM = (100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 100.0)
SUBSTRATE_WIDTH_UM = 200.0
SUBSTRATE_THICKNESS_UM = 500.0
SUBSTRATE_ORIGIN_UM = (-SUBSTRATE_WIDTH_UM / 2, -SUBSTRATE_THICKNESS_UM)
SUBSTRATE_SIZE_UM = (SUBSTRATE_WIDTH_UM, SUBSTRATE_THICKNESS_UM)
SIGNAL_WIDTH_UM = 10.0
GROUND_GAP_UM = 10.0
GROUND_WIDTH_UM = 40.0
METAL_THICKNESS_UM = 0.2
SIGNAL_ORIGIN_UM = (-SIGNAL_WIDTH_UM / 2, 0.0)
GROUND_LEFT_ORIGIN_UM = (
    -SIGNAL_WIDTH_UM / 2 - GROUND_GAP_UM - GROUND_WIDTH_UM, 0.0
)
GROUND_RIGHT_ORIGIN_UM = (SIGNAL_WIDTH_UM / 2 + GROUND_GAP_UM, 0.0)
AEDT_CORES = 4
AEDT_RAM_LIMIT_PERCENT = 80
```

The padding values are listed in public tuple order; Q2D maps them to its
native Region call internally. The unequal positive and negative Y padding in
this example is explicit model input, not a conversion convention.

Check: confirm the selected AEDT release, frequency, pass limit, padding order,
and a fresh output directory.

## 4. Build the complete cross-section {#build-cross-section}

Use PDK material records, then declare every rectangle and conductor group.
The vacuum is assigned to the Region by Q2D and does not need an authored
vacuum rectangle.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-source
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk.materials import get_material_records
from scgsim.aedt import (
    AedtResources, MatrixRunControl, PdkMaterial, Q2dConductorSpec,
    Q2dRectangleSpec, Q2dSpec, prepare_handoff,
)

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
records = get_material_records()
materials = {
    name: PdkMaterial(
        name,
        records[name]["material_kind"],
        records[name]["is_superconducting"],
        records[name]["aedt_library_name"],
    )
    for name in ("vacuum", "Si", "Nb")
}
rectangles = (
    Q2dRectangleSpec("Substrate", SUBSTRATE_ORIGIN_UM, SUBSTRATE_SIZE_UM, "Si"),
    Q2dRectangleSpec(
        "Signal", SIGNAL_ORIGIN_UM, (SIGNAL_WIDTH_UM, METAL_THICKNESS_UM), "Nb"
    ),
    Q2dRectangleSpec(
        "GroundLeft", GROUND_LEFT_ORIGIN_UM,
        (GROUND_WIDTH_UM, METAL_THICKNESS_UM), "Nb",
    ),
    Q2dRectangleSpec(
        "GroundRight", GROUND_RIGHT_ORIGIN_UM,
        (GROUND_WIDTH_UM, METAL_THICKNESS_UM), "Nb",
    ),
)
conductors = (
    Q2dConductorSpec("Signal", "SignalLine", ("Signal",), METAL_THICKNESS_UM),
    Q2dConductorSpec(
        "Ground", "ReferenceGround", ("GroundLeft", "GroundRight"),
        METAL_THICKNESS_UM,
    ),
)
```

Rectangle positions are lower-left coordinates. The signal is separated from
each ground by 10 µm; the two ground rectangles form one `ReferenceGround`.
The 500 µm substrate extends below the metal plane. The vacuum belongs to the
Region, and conductor memberships remain explicit.

Check: review each rectangle's material, origin, size, and the two declared
conductor groups against the figure.

## 5. Configure the Q2D request {#configure-the-extraction}

The Q2D frontend receives the explicit rectangle model and a matrix run
control. It does not generate a GDS slice or reuse the separate 3D Q3D model.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-config
spec = Q2dSpec(
    aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION,
    project_name=PROJECT_NAME,
    design_name=DESIGN_NAME,
    materials=materials,
    vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    rectangles=rectangles,
    conductors=conductors,
    run_control=MatrixRunControl(
        SETUP_NAME,
        frequency_ghz=FREQUENCY_GHZ,
        maximum_passes=MAXIMUM_PASSES,
    ),
    region_padding_um=REGION_PADDING_UM,
)
print(spec.to_payload())
```

Check: confirm the saved request shows the explicit AEDT version, frequency,
conductor order, rectangle membership and public padding order.

## 6. Inspect, prepare, and execute {#prepare-and-execute}

Preparation builds the solver package; the next cell executes it separately
on the licensed AEDT host. For a remote solver, transfer the complete package,
run its `run_aedt.sh` from the extracted folder, and return the complete
output directory.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-prepare
resources = AedtResources(
    cores=AEDT_CORES,
    ram_limit_percent=AEDT_RAM_LIMIT_PERCENT,
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(
    spec=spec,
    output_dir=OUTPUT_DIR,
    resources=resources,
)
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

Inspect the spec and archive before execution. A prepared package or submitted
job is not a completed result.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-execute
import subprocess

subprocess.run(
    ["bash", str(handoff.script_path)],
    cwd=handoff.run_dir,
    check=True,
)
```

AEDT Desktop runs on the same licensed host as the runner. See
[execution and handoff](../reference.qmd#execution-handoff) for the transfer
boundary.

Check: the native runner completes and the complete return is available at the
chosen output directory.

## 7. Resolve and interpret RLGC {#resolve-the-matrix}

Start a fresh analysis session and resolve the returned folder. The default
path below is the output directory prepared in step 6; for a remote run, point
it to the complete returned folder.

```{python}
#| id: line-parameter-results
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import resolve_results

RETURNED_RUN_DIR = Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-q2d")
resolved = resolve_results(RETURNED_RUN_DIR)
physics_rows = resolved.physics_results()
resolved.show_all_results(show_details=True)
physics_rows
```

The native `results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv` contains the primary C, G, L and R
blocks. Preserve their matrix labels, conductor order and native per-unit-length
units:

| Block | Native unit |
| --- | --- |
| Capacitance, C | pF/meter |
| Conductance, G | mho/meter |
| Inductance, L | nH/meter |
| Resistance, R | ohm/meter |

The resolver also reports frequency, `LastAdaptive` solution and native
status. Read the actual changes beside the intended line-model use; this page
does not convert RLGC into impedance, propagation constant, or phase velocity.

Check: the report and rows identify the returned run, conductor order, matrix
blocks, units, and native status. See the
[Q2D export contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-native-combined-matrix-export).

## 8. Adapt this notebook

Change rectangle dimensions or material records explicitly; the central cell
derives the substrate, signal and ground origins from the stated widths and
gap. Update the baseline figure if those dimensions change.
Update conductor membership when a rectangle changes role, and keep the
signal and each reference conductor unambiguous. Use a new output directory
for every preparation and retain the native matrix units when comparing runs.

Check: inspect the cross-section and serialized request before preparing the
next run. Continue to the
[Q2D backend course](../course/aedt-q2d.qmd) for family-specific detail, or
the [physical problem concept](../concepts/problems.qmd#finite-extraction-versus-a-cross-section).
